analysis:
This PR adds local, provider-side connection bookkeeping and a recovery path for connections the coordinator does not authorize.

Changes examined:
- ProviderLoop+Serve.swift: noteCoordinatorConnection is called at head lines 293, 419 and 429. Each call sits next to the existing clearConnectionAuthorization and cancelAppAttestShadow. Lease clearing on connect/disconnect (T-053, TB-011) is unchanged and still happens in the connection-control reader before work is forwarded.
- ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift (new):
  - Tracks connected/since/connections.
  - On capacity ticks, detects a connected session lacking current App Attest or legacy authorization.
  - When idle, may call requestPlannedReconnect, gated by UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.shouldReconnect (attempts, jitter, last-reconnect time).
  - lastTrustStatus is only read here, never used to grant serving. Serving authority stays with the coordinator (T-052), so no local trust elevation was found.
- ProviderLoop+Trust.swift line 104: coordinatorConnection is added to the daemon state file. It holds booleans, timestamps and a counter, with no secrets or stable identities beyond existing status data (T-058 not materially affected).
- ProviderLoop.swift lines 787-796: new state vars.

Availability: reconnect re-registers using the same fixed process X25519 key and a freshly signed attestation (makeRegistrationAttestationProvider). This does not extend any proof lifetime.

Remaining unverified contract (not in the supplied source):
- UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.shouldReconnect / connectionLacksAuthorization: their thresholds, attempt caps and backoff.
- Whether the attempt counter resets only on genuine authorization.

If these are unbounded, a coordinator that keeps refusing the connection could cause reconnect churn against the coordinator. This affects availability/DoS only, not confidentiality.

Where superviseServingAuthorization is invoked (the capacity loop) and the concurrency of requestPlannedReconnect with in-flight work were not shown. The isIdleForReregistration check covers autopilot/update only, not inference in flight; requestPlannedReconnect's drain semantics should be confirmed in integration.
